Parameters chosen at sensible thermal magnitudes: heat capacities C1=100,C2=150,C_bridge=50 J/K; conductances k_cond=10,k_bridge=5 W/K; k_rad=1e-8 so the T^4 radiative term is comparable-but-subdominant to conduction; alpha_T=1e-3 /K, T_ref=T_env=300 K; small residual losses (h_loss=0.5,A1=A2=1,h_bridge=0.2,A_bridge=0.5). dT_sat=20 K from the suggested [1,50] K range. Time window [0,60] s (~10 relaxation times at ~0.17/s) captures the full approach to a common temperature with 300 points (0.2 s resolution), resolving the new-term peak at t~2.7 s. check_substitution at the IC gives finite real -30.3 K/s.

scenario_text: Two bodies with different heat capacities are brought into thermal contact through a conducting bridge and isolated from the surroundings. Heat flows between them at a rate proportional to their instantaneous temperature difference, and both temperatures evolve until they meet at a common value. The experiment monitors each body's temperature as the pair equilibrates.
